source.notes: Human-source-first adaptation. Wrong-work-group-chat send, rapid deletion, 40+ viewers and coworker private check-in are retained as source facts. Korean wording and generic workplace staging are localized adaptations. The source author's later explanation is intentionally omitted; ending is silent embarrassment.

episode_only.identity_digest: Mid-20s Korean woman; shoulder-length straight dark-brown hair with soft inward ends and an off-center part; slightly rounded everyday face; cream short-sleeve T-shirt under a muted sage service apron, dark straight pants, slim-normal build, no glasses or jewelry; intentionally ordinary and non-glamorous.

slides.beat: A difficult customer situation becomes awkward enough that a coworker calmly steps in to help.
slides.action: worker_01 stands behind the counter visibly uncomfortable while an agitated customer gestures across the counter; a one-frame coworker calmly steps between the interaction without violence or theatrics.
scene_facts: worker_01 must use the locked episode-only identity digest and v2 drawing language
the customer is a one-frame ordinary adult extra, not threateningly villainous or physically violent
a one-frame helper coworker calmly intervenes and is visually distinct from worker_01 and all recurring leads
the location is a simple generic service counter with low-detail background
no readable menu, logo, signage, caption, dialogue, or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer immediately understands that worker_01 just had an uncomfortable customer interaction and another coworker helped.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium-wide eye-level scene from a slight side angle; worker_01 remains the emotional focus, helper coworker creates a clear spatial buffer, customer stays secondary; reserve no major text zone because this beat should read visually.

slides.beat: After the incident, worker_01 goes to a quiet staff nook and opens the messenger to tell friends about what happened.
slides.location: simple staff nook behind the workplace
slides.action: worker_01 sits alone on a small bench or stool, shoulders dropping after the tense interaction, phone in both hands as she begins typing.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity, apron, hair and clothing remain exactly continuous from slide 1
she is now alone and visibly decompressing rather than panicking
phone is present and clearly the next story object
staff nook is simple and lower-detail than the character
phone screen contains only blank/simple interface shapes; no readable text is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she is privately messaging someone after the incident.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium shot from slightly above and behind one shoulder, allowing the phone and relaxed shoulders to read while keeping a clean screen/text overlay zone.

slides.beat: She sends the message she intended for her friends.
slides.action: close insert of worker_01's hands and smartphone at the instant her thumb taps the send control; only a partial simple glimpse of her torso/apron is needed.
scene_facts: same phone, clothing and body continuity from slide 2
the phone screen provides a clean blank chat bubble area for later vector lettering
the send gesture is simple and anatomically clear with no intricate finger pose
no actual message text, chat title, app logo, or system text is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands a message has just been sent.
slides.composition: 4:5 close insert dominated by the phone and one clear thumb action; leave the upper-middle phone screen visually uncluttered for the later chat text.

slides.beat: One beat after sending, she notices the chat is the workplace group rather than her friend group.
slides.action: worker_01 jerks her gaze from the phone screen to its header area, eyes widening and body stiffening; the mistake registers instantly.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity and outfit remain continuous
the phone is angled so a clean header/title area can receive later vector lettering identifying the workplace group
her expression jumps clearly from relaxed to shocked without grotesque distortion
no readable chat title, message, caption, or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she has just realized she sent the message to the wrong group chat.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium-close reaction shot with phone in the lower foreground and face dominant; use a story-valid angle distinct from the previous insert and leave a small speech-bubble zone for the later '...어?'.

slides.beat: She immediately deletes the message, but the interface already makes it obvious that dozens of coworkers saw it.
slides.action: worker_01 rapidly operates the phone with one simple thumb while staring at a dense cluster of tiny generic read/seen indicators; panic is visible in her partial face or posture.
scene_facts: worker_01 and phone remain continuous
the interface must visually support a generic deleted-message/read-receipt concept without copying a branded app
reserve clean vector zones for a deleted-message system line and a 40-plus read indicator
the read indicators may be generic small avatar dots/icons, not recognizable recurring cast faces
no readable system text, number, message, app logo, or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she deleted it almost immediately but far too many coworkers had already seen it.
slides.composition: 4:5 close shot that keeps the phone large enough for later lettering while retaining part of worker_01's panicked face/shoulders so the frame is not only UI.

slides.beat: A coworker privately messages her asking if she is okay and what happened.
slides.action: worker_01 holds the phone frozen at chest height as a clean notification/private-message area is visually available; her face goes from panic to mortified stillness.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity and outfit remain continuous
the coworker exists only through later vector chat text; do not invent a physical second person
reserve a clean phone/notification area for two short private messages
expression is mortified and frozen, not angry or tearful
no readable DM text, sender name, caption, or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands someone from work has already privately contacted her about the accidental message.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium shot with phone slightly forward and worker_01's face fully readable; keep the upper or side phone area open for later private-message lettering.

slides.beat: She says absolutely nothing and is overwhelmed by embarrassment.
slides.action: worker_01 folds inward on the bench, torso bent, face buried in both hands or nearly hidden, shoulders raised, ears/cheeks visibly flushed; the phone remains nearby or loosely held but no new action occurs.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity, hair, apron and clothing remain continuous even with the face partly hidden
the final emotion must read as extreme embarrassment through whole-body pose rather than dialogue or narration
strong expressive pose is allowed within style; do not flatten the body language into a neutral seated pose
no reply, narration, internal monologue, reaction text, caption, message, or speech bubble appears in the final frame
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she is so embarrassed she wants to disappear, without any explanatory words.
slides.composition: 4:5 slightly high wider reaction shot showing the whole folded posture; phone is secondary; give the frame enough empty breathing room that the silent embarrassment lands visually.

set_qc: Judge the seven-frame sequence for viewer-perceived directional and compositional repetition rather than fixed left/right/front quotas.
Phone-heavy beats must still vary distance and body/face participation so S03-S06 do not become four near-identical device close-ups.
The S04 realization, S05 panic, S06 mortified freeze and S07 silent embarrassment must each read as distinct emotional states at phone size.
Replace only the minimum frame if the final set drifts toward one default three-quarter face direction or repeated camera side.
visual_direction.reflection_policy: No story-relevant mirror/reflection is required in this episode; if incidental reflections appear, keep them simple and geometrically plausible.
visual_direction.skin_color_policy: worker_01, customer and helper coworker share the same flat local-color grammar; one-frame extras must not receive an automatic yellow/orange/sepia cast.
visual_direction.notes: Seven slides are used because each slide changes the state: intervention -> private intent -> send -> wrong-chat realization -> too-late deletion/read evidence -> private check-in -> silent embarrassment.
